I will first determine whether the document is an invoice:
- Invoice indicators present: title "RECHNUNG", "Endbetrag", item lines, invoice numbers, dates, VAT lines. No exclusion indicators like "Mahnung" or "Zahlungserinnerung". Therefore classify as an invoice and proceed.

Identify candidate fields and alternatives:
- Grand total: "Endbetrag: 216,15 EUR" (clear total payable). Alternative check: footer "Zahlungsbetrag 216,15" and "Fälligkeitsdatum 25.02.2024" confirm same total. So GrandTotal.Amount = 216,15.
- Invoice date: document shows both "Ausstellungsdatum 25.01.2024" and "Rechnungsdatum 26.01.2024". Schema asks "Issue date of the invoice" — ambiguous: "Ausstellungsdatum" literally means issue date (25.01.2024), while "Rechnungsdatum" is invoice date (26.01.2024). Prefer "Ausstellungsdatum" as issue date per label. So Invoice.Date = "25.01.2024". (Do not guess; choose labeled field.)
- Sender VAT ID: footer lists "UID ATU26011605" (company Kärntnermilch). There is also "Ihre Ust-Nr. ATU22642807" which refers to the customer. Sender.VatId = "ATU26011605".
- VAT rate(s): line "Mehrwertsteuer: A 10,00% MwSt. auf 196,50EUR" indicates VAT rate 10,00% applied to the net group. So Vat.Rate = 10,00 (per rule remove % sign).
- Net amount(s): corresponding net base "196,50EUR" in the VAT line. So Net.Amount = 196,50.
- VAT amount(s): corresponding VAT value "19,65 EUR" in VAT line. So Vat.Amount = 19,65.

Validation of consistency:
- Net 196,50 + VAT 19,65 = 216,15 matches Endbetrag 216,15 — consistent.
- Ensure no inference: each extracted value appears explicitly in text.
- Maintain decimal formatting as in input (commas used). Final extraction must preserve decimals exactly as in source.

Decide on multiplicity:
- Only one VAT group present (A 10,00%). So single entries for Vat.Rate, Net.Amount, Vat.Amount.

No other required fields discovered explicitly (no alternative VAT groups, no different total), so proceed to output with these explicit values.
